evals.prompt: I just joined a new team and was handed a Python repo at ./svc-billing. Generate a newcomer quickstart page so I can ramp up.
evals.expected_output: Routes to /rui-report-quickstart create --scope ./svc-billing --out docs/reports/quickstart. Walks the scope, detects Python + (likely Django/Flask), identifies entry points + tests + docs, copies the 4-file template (templates/index.html + index.css + index.js + data.js) to <out>/, regenerates data.js with scope-derived evidence for all 7 sections, emits README.md via quickstartToMarkdown(), reports composite score and per-section verdicts.
expectations: The response invokes /rui-report-quickstart create with --scope
The response identifies the language and framework from the scope
The response describes the 7-section payload (overview, concepts, directory-map, onboarding-flow, commands, faq, further-reading)
The response mentions the 4-file template (index.html + index.css + index.js + data.js) copied from templates/
The response mentions both output artifacts: the HTML page AND README.md mirror
The response reports a composite score and per-section verdicts

evals.prompt: I need a quickstart for our open-source repo at /Users/me/projects/cli-tool. The page should be HTML and a markdown mirror so the community can fork and edit.
evals.expected_output: Routes to /rui-report-quickstart create --scope /Users/me/projects/cli-tool. The HTML page is built from the 4-file template at templates/. The README.md mirror is generated by quickstartToMarkdown() and uses identical ## headers to the HTML page in canonical 7-section order. English is the default output language.
expectations: The response invokes /rui-report-quickstart create with the absolute scope path
The response notes that the page is built from the 4-file template at templates/
The response mentions both the HTML page AND README.md as outputs
The response notes that the markdown mirror uses identical ## headers to the HTML page (via quickstartToMarkdown())
The response confirms English is the default output language
The response explains why the mirror is useful (easy to copy, edit, and publish in static sites)

evals.prompt: I want to onboard new hires onto our internal monorepo at ~/work/monorepo. Generate a quickstart — I want the page to be Chinese since most of my team reads Chinese.
evals.expected_output: Routes to /rui-report-quickstart create --scope ~/work/monorepo --language zh. The data.js labels block is swapped for the Chinese set; section structure stays canonical. All 7 sections emit Chinese content. Tone is localized, but framework names, file paths, and command names remain in their original language.
expectations: The response uses --language zh (an explicit flag, not auto-detect)
The response notes that data.js labels are swapped to Chinese and the page UI switches accordingly
The response notes that all 7 sections are emitted in Chinese
The response keeps the canonical section structure (no reordering)
The response mentions that technical terms (framework names, command names) remain in their original language
The response explains that without --language the page would default to English

evals.prompt: Run a quickstart on ./legacy-app — it's an old Java app with no README, no CONTRIBUTING, no docs folder. Just a src/ tree and a pom.xml.
evals.expected_output: Routes to /rui-report-quickstart create --scope ./legacy-app. All 7 sections render with isTodo + reason where evidence is missing (faq, further-reading will be TODO-heavy). Composite score will be low (likely D or F). The page is still generated from the 4-file template — better a TODO page than no page.
expectations: The response does NOT abort despite missing README/CONTRIBUTING/docs
The response renders all 7 sections with isTodo + reason markers for missing facets
The response notes that faq and further-reading will be TODO-heavy
The response computes a low composite score (D or F) and surfaces it in the header
The response emphasizes the no-fabrication rule: missing data renders as TODO, not invented prose

evals.prompt: I want to skip the markdown mirror — just give me the HTML page this time. Can I do that?
evals.expected_output: Yes, use --no-mirror. Routes to /rui-report-quickstart create --scope <path> --no-mirror. Only the 4 HTML/JS/CSS/data files are written; README.md is skipped. Useful when the markdown mirror would clutter the repo (e.g. embedded widgets, interactive demos).
expectations: The response confirms --no-mirror is supported
The response explains the use case (HTML-only when mirror would clutter)
The response shows the full command line including --no-mirror
The response notes that the 4 HTML/JS/CSS/data files are still emitted even with --no-mirror

evals.prompt: Generate a quickstart for ./my-app but I want the directory map to go 4 levels deep instead of the default 3.
evals.expected_output: Routes to /rui-report-quickstart create --scope ./my-app --depth 4. The directory-map section's tree annotates the top 4 levels (vs default 3); data.js directory-map.depth = 4. Other 6 sections unchanged.
expectations: The response uses --depth 4
The response notes that only the directory-map section is affected
The response explains the trade-off (deeper maps are more informative but noisier)

evals.prompt: Why does the report have a composite score and per-section verdicts? What's the grading scale?
evals.expected_output: The report is a self-assessment of how well the project teaches a newcomer. Per-section verdict is pass (≥0.90, ✅), partial (0.50–0.89, ⚠️), or fail (<0.50, 🚫). Composite = mean(coverage) × 100. Grade: A≥90, B≥75, C≥60, D≥40, F<40. The data.js schema exposes computeScore(sections) that derives all three. Low scores surface a call-to-action: 'fill the TODO markers to improve your onboarding'.
expectations: The response explains the per-section verdict thresholds (pass / partial / fail)
The response explains the composite score formula (mean × 100)
The response lists the grade scale (A / B / C / D / F)
The response frames the score as a self-assessment of onboarding quality, not code quality
The response notes that data.js computeScore() is the helper that derives score, grade, and per-section verdicts

evals.prompt: I notice the page has a sidebar with reading-progress, sidebar, topbar, etc. — does this quickstart use the same 9-region layout as docs/quickstart/?
evals.expected_output: No. rui-report-quickstart uses the 4-file template at templates/ (data.js + index.html + index.css + index.js) — a single-column newcomer page with a header, score banner, 7 stacked sections, and a footer. It does NOT use the docs/quickstart/ 9-region layout. The two skills are complementary: rui-docs-quickstart is a maintainer manual, while rui-report-quickstart generates a newcomer-facing guide for any local project.
expectations: The response clarifies that rui-report-quickstart uses the 4-file template, not the docs/quickstart/ 9-region layout
The response explains that the primary contract is the 7-section onboarding report rather than a specific internal file split
The response distinguishes the two skills: rui-docs-quickstart is a maintainer manual; rui-report-quickstart is a newcomer-facing page generator

evals.prompt: I ran a quickstart yesterday and edited README.md to add a FAQ entry. Today I re-ran. Will my edit survive?
evals.expected_output: By default, no — regenerated outputs overwrite the previous README.md body. The 4 file templates (index.html, index.css, index.js) and the canonical ## section headers are byte-stable, so a re-run produces a structurally compatible file. The data.js (which carries the actual content) is regenerated from scope evidence, so a hand-edited FAQ entry is overwritten unless it is also discoverable from the scope. As a workaround, keep custom additions in a separate file and merge them back after the run, or extend the FAQ source so the entry is re-detected.
expectations: The response acknowledges that re-running overwrites the markdown mirror body
The response notes that the 4-file template is byte-stable so the HTML page re-renders cleanly
The response notes that section ## headers are stable across re-runs
The response suggests a workaround (separate file, manual merge, or extend the FAQ source so the entry is re-detected)

evals.prompt: I'm worried the analyzer will hallucinate — what stops it from inventing file paths that aren't in my repo?
evals.expected_output: The no-fabrication rule explicitly forbids inventing file paths. Every claim in the 7 sections must cite a real file/line/symbol from the scope or render as isTodo: true with a reason. The HTML page surfaces TODO sections as a yellow badge with the reason; the README.md mirror renders the same sections as a `> TODO — <reason>` blockquote. Verdicts drop for any section that has TODO markers. The composite score reflects this — high TODO count = low score = call-to-action to fill them in.
expectations: The response cites the no-fabrication rule explicitly
The response explains the TODO marker convention (isTodo + reason) in both the HTML page and the markdown mirror
The response notes that verdicts and the composite score penalize heavy TODO use
The response frames the score as a self-audit mechanism

evals.prompt: What 7 sections does the quickstart cover and in what order?
evals.expected_output: Canonical 7 sections in this order: 1) Project Overview (overview), 2) Key Concepts (concepts), 3) Directory Map (directory-map), 4) Onboarding Flow (onboarding-flow), 5) Command Cheatsheet (commands), 6) FAQ (faq), 7) Further Reading (further-reading). The order is fixed by the canonicalSections array in templates/data.js; the page does no reordering. Section slugs are the canonical identifiers used in data.js and the markdown mirror's ## headers.
expectations: The response lists all 7 sections by name and slug
The response preserves the canonical order (overview → concepts → directory-map → onboarding-flow → commands → faq → further-reading)
The response notes that the order is fixed by canonicalSections in data.js and not subject to reordering

evals.prompt: What's the difference between rui-report-quickstart, rui-report-files, rui-report-diagram, and rui-report-test?
evals.expected_output: They are complementary report skills with different outputs: rui-report-files analyzes file size and coupling, rui-report-diagram produces architecture diagrams, rui-report-test generates a six-scene repo health report, and rui-report-quickstart creates a seven-section newcomer quickstart. All four use the 4-file template layout (data.js + index.html + index.css + index.js) under templates/ so the catalog renders consistently. quickstart's primary contract is the 7-section onboarding output (with optional README.md mirror via quickstartToMarkdown()).
expectations: The response notes that quickstart is defined by its 7-section onboarding contract + the 4-file template
The response distinguishes each skill by its output (size report / diagram / test / quickstart)
The response notes that all four skills share the 4-file template pattern
The response clarifies that the 4 are complementary

evals.prompt: If I just run `/rui-report-quickstart create` with no flags at all, what language will the page be in?
evals.expected_output: English. The default language is `en` and there is no auto-detect from the user's prompt. To switch to Chinese, pass `--language zh` explicitly. The data.js `meta.language` field reflects the resolved language; the labels block in data.js carries the per-language UI strings.
expectations: The response confirms English is the default
The response notes there is no auto-detect — the user must pass --language explicitly
The response explains the data.js mechanism (meta.language + labels block)

evals.prompt: I want to ship the quickstart under docs/reports/quickstart/ but my repo is a multi-package monorepo with no clear top-level entry point. How will the report handle that?
evals.expected_output: The skill walks the scope with standard exclusions, then renders all 7 sections from the evidence it finds. The overview section's stack + scope tiles will reflect whatever manifests are present (e.g. a workspace package.json). The directory-map will show the top-level structure. The concepts and onboarding-flow sections will degrade to TODO when no stable modules or entry points surface. The composite score will reflect the gaps.
expectations: The response notes that the report handles monorepos by walking the scope + using whatever manifests exist
The response notes that some sections will degrade to TODO when no stable entry points surface
The response does not promise full coverage for monorepos — it frames the score as a self-audit
